searchText: > On line 41/42 contracts start with `0xff` which is selfdestruct. Are those data contracts? <@!425279588009246720> Even if it was a data contract, surely starting a contract (really just a data blob) with 0xff is bad idea. If someone sent a transaction to the contract, wouldn't the self desctruct opcode execute and then the contract would be deleted...? Or am i missing something obvious? un/fortunately, those contracts have 0 balance. But this together with the state rent changes would have been an interesting development > If someone sent a transaction to the contract, wouldn't the self desctruct opcode execute Nope, selfdestruct pops one item off the stack, so it would error out on that So a 'random data' contract would have to have something like `NUMBER/TIMESTAMP/PC ; SELFDESTRUCT` for that to happen, which lowers the likelihood (a bit) > lot of them may have a valid first opcode (but would halt anyway, such as CODECOPY as first instruction) I filtered out most of those already, but I missed some, e.g. `CODECOPY` (what I meant by "and filtering a bit more aggressively on the first (a few slipped by me)") Is it possible these data contracts are used via `EXTCODECOPY`? That's the only way they are used 🙂 It became more prevalent after 1884 which raised SLOAD costs and for longer data it is worth using data contracts. > To continue from previous room: I'm analyzing all contract code at block `9666637`. I dumped out all code (22G), and am now doing a filtering: only code containing > > - At least one `JUMP` or `JUMPI`, > - At least one `BEGINSUB` (0xB2) > - And a `JUMPDEST` _after_ the `BEGINSUB` <@!211091239112671234> The `JUMPDEST BEGINSUB JUMP` is also invalid Looks I'm late to the party... Here's the metadata checking hack I used: https://gist.github.com/axic/aaee2f0252d519d9adde0bb83a7c0524 <@!259648573401071617> here's one of the first relevant comments (and there's more analysis later on) on the 1884 vs. data contracts topic: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-1884-repricing-for-trie-size-dependent-opcodes/3024/35?u=axic > JUMPDEST BEGINSUB JUMP is also invalid right... I guess the analysis left out half of the cases 😦 <@425274498732916736> wait. How would you get to the wrong side of the beginsub in the first place if there isn't a jump across it to begin with? JUMPSUB? Yeah but in that case it's broken today So no need to worry about breaking it > <@!425274498732916736> wait. How would you get to the wrong side of the beginsub in the first place if there isn't a jump across it to begin with? <@!211091239112671234> Seems correct. So what to do with the remaining codes? The list from me still needs to be cleared from "obviously broken"/data contracts. Then probably need to look at one (the shortest) to see if beginsub changes anything.

excerpts.author: _drinkcoffee
excerpts.content:
> On line 41/42 contracts start with `0xff` which is selfdestruct. Are those data contracts?
<@!425279588009246720> Even if it was a data contract, surely starting a contract (really just a data blob) with 0xff is bad idea. If someone sent a transaction to the contract, wouldn't the self desctruct opcode execute and then the contract would be deleted...? Or am i missing something obvious?

excerpts.author: hmijail
excerpts.content: un/fortunately, those contracts have 0 balance. But this together with the state rent changes would have been an interesting development

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
>  If someone sent a transaction to the contract, wouldn't the self desctruct opcode execute

Nope, selfdestruct pops one item off the stack, so it would error out on that

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: So a 'random data' contract would have to have something like `NUMBER/TIMESTAMP/PC ; SELFDESTRUCT` for that to happen, which lowers the likelihood (a bit)

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
>  lot of them may have a valid first opcode (but would halt anyway, such as CODECOPY as first instruction) 
I filtered out most of those already, but I missed some, e.g. `CODECOPY` (what I meant by "and filtering a bit more aggressively on the first (a few slipped by me)")

excerpts.author: s1na
excerpts.content: Is it possible these data contracts are used via  `EXTCODECOPY`?

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content: That's the only way they are used 🙂

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content: It became more prevalent after 1884 which raised SLOAD costs and for longer data it is worth using data contracts.
